subject: MAP: Technical evaluation gating, shortlist, and milestone owners
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthgrid.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation gating, shortlist, and milestone owners

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call earlier. Per our discussion, I’m drafting the MAP milestone for the technical evaluation and wanted to confirm alignment on scope, owners, and what will constitute an acceptance gate. I pasted a concise proposal below and attached a living MAP workbook (healthgrid_map_draft.xlsx) and a short tech-eval checklist (hg_eval_checklist.md).

Proposed technical evaluation milestone (target completion: 2026-06-11)
- Objective: Validate Redwood meets HealthGrid latency and cost SLOs while matching accuracy baseline on the clinical summarization task.
- Success criteria (all must be met):
  - Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for 256-token prompts under 2 concurrent workers (baseline workload simulation attached)
  - Cost: tokenized cost no more than $0.006/token equivalent for steady-state batch sizes (we'll translate to your usage pattern)
  - Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.68 and no more than 12% clinically significant hallucinations on the evaluation prompt set
- Model shortlist for benchmarks: Llama-3-70B Q4, Mistral-Instruct-22B, Redwood-FT-13B (quantized variants to be tested)
- Deliverables: benchmark runbook, raw logs (latency/cost), evaluation report with sample outputs and failure analysis
- Owners: HealthGrid provides evaluation prompt set and clinical rubric (Samira/Tom). Redwood to provide runbook, benchmark scripts, and perform two controlled runs (Rafael lead, Ben supporting).
- Dependencies: shared dataset, test credentials to Redwood Dedicated sandbox, scheduling 8-hour run window for stable load testing.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Samira/Tom: confirm the proposed success criteria and shortlist or suggest models you want added/removed by EOD Monday (2026-05-17).
2) HealthGrid: share the masked evaluation prompt set (or a synthetic equivalent) and target throughput profile.
3) Redwood (Rafael/Ben): prepare an execution plan and a draft runbook by 2026-05-18.

If that looks good I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet and propose milestone dates in the workbook. Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can lock in the Dedicated sandbox time.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: healthgrid_map_draft.xlsx (XLSX - 45KB)]
[Attachment: hg_eval_checklist.md (MD - 8KB)]

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthgrid.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 18:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation gating, shortlist, and milestone owners

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear summary and the checklist — this is helpful. Quick responses inline:
- Success criteria: the latency and ROUGE targets look reasonable. We’d like to relax cost constraint a bit during the first run (up to $0.007/token) to allow for non-optimized quantized runs; ultimate target should remain $0.006.
- Shortlist: please add OpenAssistant-XL to the shortlist; our research team is curious about its behavior on clinical text.
- Owners: confirmed — I’ll share the redacted prompt set by COB Monday (2026-05-17).
- Sandbox access: we need a short checklist for security controls for test credentials before we provision access (SOC2 evidence stub would be great).

We are aligned on the 2026-06-11 milestone but if early results suggest more tuning we may request an extension.

Best,
Samira
Director, Applied ML — HealthGrid
[Attachment: hg_security_requirements.pdf (PDF - 72KB)]

Rafael — can you draft the runbook outline and list of required artifacts for the sandbox (TLS certs, ip allowlist, test user accounts, logging hooks)? I’d like a short internal sync Monday morning; can you both be available 9:30am PT?

Thanks — Camila

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation gating, shortlist, and milestone owners

Camila / Ben —

I drafted the runbook outline and uploaded to the shared Drive link (see related_links). Highlights:
- Benchmark harness: containerized runner with deterministic seeds, traffic replay for p95 measurement, and token accounting hooks.
- Security prechecks for sandbox: ephemeral API keys, IP allowlist, audit logging enabled to the customer log sink, and access expiry after 72 hours. I attached a short SOC2 evidence stub we can share; Ben please review for any gaps.
- Execution plan: two benchmark passes (baseline config, and quantized/optimized config) with result reconciliation and failure triage.

Ben — can you confirm which quantized builds you recommend we run first and provide a rough GPU-hour estimate so I can book the Dedicated pool?

Rafael
Principal Applied ML — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_soc2_stub.pdf (PDF - 24KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 15 May 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation gating, shortlist, and milestone owners

Quick update —
- Model builds: ready to run Llama-3-70B Q4 (FP16, 8-bit quant), Mistral-Instruct-22B (6-bit quant), Redwood-FT-13B (4-bit PTQ), and OpenAssistant-XL (FP16).
- Estimated runs: ~6 hours per model variant for the full evaluation set at our baseline throughput (~2 concurrent workers). GPU-hours estimate: ~36 GPU-hours for single-pass baseline; 72 GPU-hours if we run optimized quantized configs as a second pass.
- I’ll prepare a short run schedule and post it to the Drive; Rafael, once you confirm the sandbox checklist I’ll reserve the Dedicated pool for 6/02–6/03 as a tentative block.

Samira — I’ll follow up with bulletized notes on any model caveats we observe on clinical text after the first pass.

Thanks,
Ben
Staff SW/ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
